5788               	; 			' THE BALL IS ON THE GROUND WHEN HE GETS TO IT.
5789               	; 			'
5790               	; 			' The bounce phase used to be `lx AND 31` -- a byte out of
5791               	; 			' the placement table, which is to say arbitrary. Run onto
5792               	; 			' a screen and the first ball might be at the bottom of its
5793               	; 			' arc, where a jump clears it, or at the top, where it has
5794               	; 			' to be ducked, and nothing on the way in told you which.
5795               	; 			' Sometimes you could keep running and jump it; sometimes
5796               	; 			' the same approach at the same speed could not be jumped
5797               	; 			' at all. That is not difficulty, it is a coin toss.
5798               	; 			'
5799               	; 			' So the phase is worked BACKWARDS from the meeting. He
5800               	; 			' closes 4 px a pass and the ball 2, so they meet in
5801               	; 			' (gap / 6) passes; the phase advances one a pass and wraps
5802               	; 			' at 32, so seeding it with the NEGATIVE of that lands it on
5803               	; 			' phase 0 -- the ground -- exactly as they arrive.
5804               	; 			'
5805               	; 			' The gap is the same either way round: he enters at one
5806               	; 			' wall and the ball starts `stag` in from the other, so it
5807               	; 			' is 232 - stag whichever direction the floor runs.
5808               	; 			'
5809               	; 			' It stays forgiving rather than exact. The arc is flat near
5810               	; 			' the bottom, so anything within eight passes either side is
5811               	; 			' still under the jump; and it only holds for an unbroken
5812               	; 			' run, which is the case the player is entitled to read off
5813               	; 			' the screen. Duck, stop or take a hit and everything after
5814               	; 			' is out of step again -- which is the game.
5815               	; 			' obp is a BALL-only field: upd_obst reads it under an
5816               	; 			' IF uk = OB_BALL and nothing else touches it, and every
5817               	; 			' ball has it computed below. It was seeded here from a
5818               	; 			' table byte that no longer exists, and for anything but
5819               	; 			' a ball that seed was never read.
5820               	; 			IF lk = OB_BALL THEN

     BE2E 21F4

6782               	; 		' HE IS STANDING ON A STEP, so he moves at the STEP's rate: 2 px
6783               	; 		' across and 1 up PER PASS -- the staircase's own slope, and exactly
6784               	; 		' what one phase of esc_tick moves the pattern by.
6785               	; 		'
6786               	; 		' NOT `fdv`, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. Everything else in this loop
6787               	; 		' is paced by the frame delta, and pacing him that way too made him
6788               	; 		' outrun the steps the moment a pass cost more than one frame: his
6789               	; 		' feet started planted on a tread and ended floating above it.
6790               	; 		' Pacing the ANIMATION by fdv instead is worse -- four phases cannot
6791               	; 		' be stepped by 2 or 3 without aliasing, and the staircase runs
6792               	; 		' backwards (see esc_tick). The only arrangement that cannot drift
6793               	; 		' is the one where both are driven by the same fixed step, so the
6794               	; 		' rider is clocked by the pass, like the steps he is standing on.
6795               	; 		'
6796               	; 		' THE FIRST FEW PASSES ARE THE STEP ON. Walking on, his feet are on
6797               	; 		' the floor and the bottom tread is 4 to 7 px above them, so he
6798               	; 		' climbs at 2 px a pass until he catches it (the tread is rising at
6799               	; 		' 1, so the gap closes at 1 a pass) and then rides with it. Jumping
6800               	; 		' on he lands ON a tread, so eson is 0 and this never runs.

7338               	; 		' a short step, it reads as the controls being ignored, and it is
7339               	; 		' worst exactly where a player taps rather than holds: lining up a
7340               	; 		' jump, or edging around a hazard.

8261               	;
8262               	; 	' THE VICTROLA, AS CHARACTERS. It never moves, so a sprite spent a
8263               	; 	' scan-line slot on something that can be painted once when the screen is
8264               	; 	' drawn -- and at one 16x16 sprite it could only ever be one colour and
8265               	; 	' one size. Four cells is twice the area for no sprite at all.
8266               	; 	'
8267               	; 	' It stands ON the slab, so it fills the band's rows 2 and 3; row 4 is
8268               	; 	' the floor bar itself -- and a PRIZE uses those same two rows.
8269               	; 	'
8270               	; 	' THEY CAN SHARE A BAND, AND THE CLAIM THAT USED TO BE HERE WAS WRONG.
8271               	; 	' It said the two never share a screen because "genstore keeps prizes off
8272               	; 	' the screens that carry hazards". That stopped being true the moment
8273               	; 	' hazard placement moved into the per-Krook stor_lvl table, and nothing
8274               	; 	' noticed, because the prize table is not part of the level table and
8275               	; 	' every check was written about one object at a time. Two money bags ended
8276               	; 	' up standing on a radio -- not fighting it, since the two routines poke
8277               	; 	' different cells and the later writer simply wins, so they read as one
8278               	; 	' merged object.
8279               	; 	'
8280               	; 	' WHAT KEEPS THEM APART IS COLUMNS. A radio stands at column 7, 15 or 23
8281               	; 	' (see lrc below); genstore's _off_the_rack nudges a prize clear of all
8282               	; 	' three, and checklevels.py reads that arithmetic back out of THIS file
8283               	; 	' and fails the build on any overlap.
8284               	; 	'
8285               	; 	' rdall = 1 paints all four cells, 0 repaints only the top-right one --
8286               	; 	' the pulse. Same address arithmetic either way, so the two cannot drift.
8287               	; 	' A BEAM TOP HANGS OUT OF THE FLOOR ABOVE, and the beam it belongs to has
8288               	; 	' just been taken away. `beam_tops` stamps SLABP -- the floor bar with the
8289               	; 	' support carried up through its lower three pixel rows -- into the slab
8290               	; 	' row above every pillar, and it runs BEFORE the radios and prizes are
8291               	; 	' placed. Clearing a pillar's own cells therefore left three grey pixels
8292               	; 	' dangling from the ceiling with nothing under them.
8293               	; 	'
8294               	; 	' TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: only SLABP is put back to SLAB. The row above the
8295               	; 	' top shopping floor is the ROOF DECK, a different character altogether,
8296               	; 	' and writing a floor bar over it would punch a hole in the roof.
8297               	; 	' A SHELF RUN IS FIVE CELLS WIDE and a radio covers two, so one standing
8298               	; 	' on a counter punched a hole through its middle and left the ends either
8299               	; 	' side -- the same incoherence the dangling pillar had, and worse, because
8300               	; 	' a counter reads as one object. The whole unit goes: walk outward along
8301               	; 	' the band's row 2 while the cell is still a shelf top, clearing it and
8302               	; 	' its bottom half together.
8303               	; 	'
8304               	; 	' Bounded at eight steps. The runs are five, so eight is slack rather
8305               	; 	' than a guess -- and an unbounded walk would run off the end of the row
8306               	; 	' if the name table ever held something unexpected.
8307               	; 	#if NES
8308               	; 	' WHAT THE TEMPLATE PUT IN THIS CELL, for a target that cannot read its
8309               	; 	' own video memory back. #nta is the offset INSIDE the band (0-159) and
8310               	; 	' nbl is the band; the answer is the byte SCREEN blitted there.
8311               	; 	'
8312               	; 	' This is the same arithmetic the blit itself does in draw_band --
8313               	; 	' template id out of stor_ix for (band, screen), times 160, plus the
8314               	; 	' offset -- so the two cannot disagree about what is on screen. It is
8315               	; 	' reading what the cell MEANS, not guessing from where the cell is: a
8316               	; 	' coordinate is a fact about this layout, the character is a fact about
8317               	; 	' the world, and only the second is safe to erase on.
8318               	; nes_tpl:
8319               	; 	nti = lv8(nbl)
8320               	; 	nti = nti + klsc
8321               	; 	#ntb = #stix + nti
8322               	; 	ntd = PEEK(#ntb)
8323               	; 	#ntc = #tsrc(ntd)
8324               	; 	#ntc = #ntc + #nta
8325               	; 	#ntc = #ntc + #sttp
8326               	; 	ntv = PEEK(#ntc)
8327               	; 	RETURN
8328               	; 	#endif
8329               	;

9053               	; upd_obst:

9055               	; 	' ONE ACCUMULATOR PER KIND, NOT PER SLOT. Every hazard of a kind moves at
9056               	; 	' that kind's speed, so three calls a pass serve all eight slots.
9057               	; 	'
9058               	; 	' Per-slot would have meant up to eight calls of O(fdv) work every pass --
9059               	; 	' the positive feedback loop CLAUDE.md 3A warns about, where a slow pass is
9060               	; 	' made slower by the very code meant to take the loop rate out of the
9061               	; 	' game's behaviour. It also saves the eight bytes an obacc() would cost,
9062               	; 	' and ColecoVision RAM is the tighter budget.
9063               	; 	pacc = oacb

9353               	;
9354               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
9355               	; 	'
9356               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
9357               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
9358               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
9359               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
9360               	; 	'
9361               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
9362               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
9363               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
9364               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9365               	; 	'
9366               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
9367               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
9368               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
9369               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
9370               	; 	'
9371               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
9372               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
9373               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
9374               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
9375               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for
9376               	; 	' a genuine stall and at five it only fires for one.

9865               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9866               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9867               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9868               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9869               	; 	' runs every pass.
9870               	; 	'
9871               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9872               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9873               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9874               	; 	'
9875               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9876               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9877               	; 	'
9878               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9879               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9880               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9881               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9882               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9883               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9884               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9885               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9886               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9887               	; 	'
9888               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9889               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9890               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9891               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9892               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9893               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9894               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9895               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
9896               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
9897               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
9898               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the

9900               	; 	'

9996               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9997               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9998               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9999               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
10000               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
10001               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
10002               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
10003               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
10004               	; 	'
10005               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
10006               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
10007               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
10008               	; 	'
10009               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
10010               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
10011               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
10012               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
10013               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
10014               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
10015               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
10016               	; 	'
10017               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
10018               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
10019               	; 	'
10020               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
10021               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
10022               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
10023               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
10024               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
10025               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
10026               	; 	'

10030               	; 	' before any of this.

10501               	;
10502               	; 	' ======================================================================
10503               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10504               	; 	' ======================================================================
10505               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10506               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10507               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10508               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10509               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10510               	; 	'
10511               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10512               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10513               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10514               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10515               	; 	' broken.
10516               	; 	'
10517               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10518               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10519               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10520               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10521               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10522               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10523               	; 	'
10524               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10525               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10526               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10527               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10528               	; coll_obst:
10529               cvb_COLL_OBST
10530               	; 	IF klst = ST_ESC THEN RETURN		' riding is invincible, per the
10531 DF36 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLST,r0
     DF38 21C2

     DF3C 0300

10535 DF42 0460  28 	b @cv656
     DF44 DF4A

10863               	; 	' ONE PASS LONGER THAN THE SOUND, because the sound does not start here.
10864               	; 	' sfh is a latch that sfx_tick consumes on the NEXT pass, so the note
10865               	; 	' runs passes 2..HITSND+1 of the freeze and this ends with it.
10866               	; 	hfz = HITSND + 1

     E1F0 1500     
10868 E1F2 D800  38 	movb r0,@cvb_HFZ
     E1F4 21A0     
10869               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10870               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10871               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10872               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10873               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10874               	; 	' away from.
10875               	; 	'
10876               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10877               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10878               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10879               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10880               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10881               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10882               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10883               	; 	'
10884               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10885               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10886               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10887               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10888               	; 	'
10889               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10890               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10891               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10892               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10893               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10894               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10895               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10896               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10897               	; 	'
10898               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10899               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.
10900               	; 	IF klst <> ST_JUMP THEN

     E1F8 21C2

     E1FC 0100

11058               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
11059               	; 	'
11060               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
11061               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
11062               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
11063               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
11064               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
11065               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
11066               	; 	'
11067               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
11068               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
11069               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
11070               	; 	'
11071               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
11072               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
11073               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
11074               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
11075               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
11076               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
11077               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

11183               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.
11184               	; 	'
11185               	; 	' This test used to sit AFTER his sprites had been written, so every pass
11186               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
11187               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11188               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11189               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11190               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11191               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11192               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
11193               	; 	'
11194               	; 	' Deciding BEFORE drawing costs one test and cannot race the ISR at all:
11195               	; 	' the mirror never holds a position to be caught with.
11196               	; 	IF klst = ST_ELEV THEN

11245               cv730
11246               	; 	' KELLY'S HAT DOES NOT FLASH WHEN HE IS HIT. It used to alternate to white
11247               	; 	' on the `fphs AND 2` phase for the twenty frames of `knock`, on the
11248               	; 	' argument that nothing else on screen said nine seconds had just gone.
11249               	; 	' That argument no longer holds: the knockback still throws him, the HUD's
11250               	; 	' digits still drop by nine, and the hit now has a sound that is allowed to
11251               	; 	' finish. Three signals for one event, and the flash was the least legible
11252               	; 	' of them -- a two-frame colour swap on a 16 px hat, during the one moment
11253               	; 	' the player is looking at where they are being pushed.
11254               	; 	'
11255               	; 	' Dropping it retires `kcol` with it: the hat is C_KHAT always, so the
11256               	; 	' colour goes straight into the SPRITE calls below and the per-pass
11257               	; 	' variable, its assignment and two nested IFs all go.
11258               	; 	'
11259               	; 	' `knock` STAYS. It is the knockback, which is the part that is felt.
11260               	; 	' KELLY IS SPRITES 0, 1 AND 2 and nothing else ever is -- the VDP drops
11261               	; 	' the highest-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so the lowest
11262               	; 	' slots are the ones that can never disappear, and the player is the one
11263               	; 	' thing that must never disappear.
11264               	; 	'
11265               	; 	' THE BAND SPRITES SHARE A y ON PURPOSE. Slots 0 and 1 both sit at ky and
11266               	; 	' between them cover rows 0-15; slot 2 sits at ky+16. Boxes 0/1 and box 2
11267               	; 	' never share a scanline, so an actor costs at most TWO boxes on any line
11268               	; 	' -- and the VDP counts boxes, not pixels, so an empty overlap would have
11269               	; 	' cost just as much as a full one. Two actors meeting is four, exactly
11270               	; 	' the per-line limit, which is why obstacles are suppressed on Harry's
11271               	; 	' floor rather than merely being a kindness.
11272               	; 	ky = flry(klv)
11273 E48E D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLV,r0

11417               	; 		' divide -- `/` compiles to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and
11418               	; 		' this is per-frame code. Two adjacent bits give 0,4,8,12.

11420               	; 		' KELLY USES BITS 2 AND 3 AND HARRY USES 3 AND 4, because a stride
11421               	; 		' has to cover about a stride's worth of ground or the figure
11422               	; 		' skates. Kelly runs 4 px a frame, so four frames a pose is 16 px;
11423               	; 		' Harry runs 1.75, so eight frames a pose is 14. Matching the two
11424               	; 		' rates to the two speeds is what keeps both looking like running.

11431               	; 		' beat an odometer would have flipped his legs every single pass at

12261               	;
12262               	; 	' ======================================================================
12263               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12264               	; 	' ======================================================================
12265               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12266               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12267               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12268               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12269               	; 	'
12270               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12271               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12272               	; 	'
12273               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12274               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12275               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12276               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12277               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12278               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12279               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12280               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12281               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12282               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12283               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12284               	; esc_tick:
12285               cvb_ESC_TICK
12286               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
12287               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12288               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12289               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12290               	; 	IF klsc > 0 THEN
12291 EC1E D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0

12309               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12310               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12311               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12312               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12313               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12314               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12315               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12316               	; 	'
12317               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12318               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12319               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12320               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12321               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12322               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12323               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.
12324               	; 	escp = escp + 1

12620               	;
12621               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12622               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12623               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12624               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12625               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12626               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12627               	; 	'
12628               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12629               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12630               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12631               	; 	'
12632               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12633               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12634               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12635               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12636               	; 	'
12637               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12638               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12639               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12640               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12641               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12642               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12643               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12644               	; 	'
12645               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12646               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12647               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12648               	; 	'
12649               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12650               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12651               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.
12652               	; scan_furn:
12653               cvb_SCAN_FURN

13005               	;
13006               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
13007               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
13008               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
13009               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
13010               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
13011               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13012               	; scan_wipe:
13013               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
13014               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
13015               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
13016               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
13017               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
13018               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
13019               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
13020               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
13021               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
13022               	; 	'
13023               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
13024               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
13025               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
13026               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
13027               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one

13123               	; 	' THE TWO ACTORS ARE SPRITES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS CHARACTERS.
13124               	; 	'
13125               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
13126               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
13127               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
13128               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour

13130               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
13131               	; 	'

13133               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers

13135               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.

13139               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
13140               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.

13931               	;
13932               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13933               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13934               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13935               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13936               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13937               	; 	'
13938               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13939               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13940               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13941               	; 	'
13942               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13943               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13944               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13945               	; 	'
13946               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13947               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13948               	; 	'
13949               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13950               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13951               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13952               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13953               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13954               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13955               	; 	'
13956               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13957               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13958               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13959               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13960               	; 	'
13961               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13962               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13963               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13964               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
13965               	; bonus_count:

14081               	;
14082               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14083               	; 	'
14084               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14085               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14086               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14087               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14088               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14089               	; 	'
14090               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14091               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14092               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14093               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14094               	; 	' counting stops.
14095               	;
14096               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14097               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14098               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14099               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14100               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14101               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14102               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14103               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14104               	; 	'
14105               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14106               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14107               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
14108               	;

14407               	;
14408               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14409               	; 	'
14410               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14411               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14412               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14413               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14414               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14415               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14416               	; 	'
14417               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14418               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14419               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14420               	; 	'
14421               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14422               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14423               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14424               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14425               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14426               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14427               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14428               	; 	'
14429               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14430               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14431               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14432               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14433               	; 	'
14434               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14435               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14436               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14437               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14438               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14439               	; 	'
14440               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14441               	; 	' did not finish.
14442               	; pause_beat:
14443               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

14804               cv969
14805               	;
14806               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14807               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14808               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14809               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14810               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14811               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14812               	;
14813               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14814               	; 	'
14815               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14816               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14817               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14818               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14819               	; 	'
14820               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14821               	; 	'
14822               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14823               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14824               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14825               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14826               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14827               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14828               	; 	'
14829               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14830               	; 	'
14831               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14832               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14833               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14834               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14835               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14836               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14837               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14838               	; 	'
14839               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
14840               	; 	'
14841               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
14842               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
14843               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
14844               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
14845               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
14846               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
14847               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
14848               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
14849               	; 	'
14850               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
14851               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
14852               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
14853               	; 	'
14854               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
14855               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
14856               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
14857               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
14858               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
14859               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
14860               	; 	'

14863               	; 	'
14864               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14865               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14866               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14867               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14868               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14869               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14870               	; 	'
14871               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14872               	; 	'
14873               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14874               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14875               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14876               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14877               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14878               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not

15078               	;
15079               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
15080               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
15081               	; 	'
15082               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
15083               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
15084               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
15085               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
15086               	; 	'
15087               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
15088               	; 	'
15089               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
15090               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
15091               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
15092               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
15093               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
15094               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
15095               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
15096               	; 	'
15097               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
15098               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
15099               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
15100               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
15101               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
15102               	; 	'
15103               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
15104               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
15105               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
15106               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
15107               	; 	#if TI994A
15108               	; 	BANK 2
15109      0184     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15247               	;
15248               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
15249               	; 	'
15250               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
15251               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
15252               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
15253               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
15254               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
15255               	; 	'
15256               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
15257               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
15258               	;
15259               	; font_col:
15260               cvb_FONT_COL
15261               	; 	DATA BYTE $14,$14,$14,$14,$14,$14,$14,$14	' space
15262 6202 1414     	byte >14,>14,>14,>14,>14,>14,>14,>14
     6204 1414     
     6206 1414

15773               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15774               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15775               	; 	'
15776               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15777               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15778               	; 	' being small sprites.
15779               	; 	'
15780               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15781               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15782               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15783               	; 	'
15784               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15785               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15786               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15787               	;
15788               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15789               cvb_SPR_KELLY

17029               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
17030               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
17031               	; 	'
17032               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
17033               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
17034               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
17035               	; 	'
17036               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
17037               	; 	' blit is
17038               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
17039               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
17040               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
17041               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
17042               	; 	'
17043               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
17044               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
17045               	; 	'
17046               	; 	' template ids:
17047               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
17048               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
17049               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
17050               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
17051               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
17052               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
17053               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
17054               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
